 Published  November 20, 2026 7:42 PM EST Food recalls: What prompts them and what you should know 
 Dr.  Kimberly Baker, a food systems and safety program team director for Clemson Cooperative Extension shared what kicks off a food recall and what consumers can do to stay up to date on food safety in the U.S. (Credit: AP Campus Insights/Kimberly Baker, Clemson University)
 The Brief
 About 229,430 CLC and Johnson Level products are being recalled because children can access their button cell batteries, posing a risk of serious injury or death if swallowed. 
 The recalled products include lighted portfolios, digital angle locators, calipers and calculators sold at major hardware retailers and online, including Amazon. 
 Consumers should stop using the products, keep them away from children and contact Hultafors Group North America for a refund. No injuries or incidents have been reported. 
 More than 229,000 trade tools sold at major hardware retailers and online are being recalled because their button cell batteries can be accessed by children, posing an ingestion hazard, federal safety officials announced.
 The recall was  announced by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) on Nov. 19.
 Tools recalled over safety standards
 Big picture view:
 The recall involves Custom Leather Craft (CLC) Lighted Portfolios and several Johnson Level & Tool digital products, including digital angle locators, digital calipers and building calculators.
 According to the CPSC, the products violate mandatory safety standards for consumer products containing button cell and coin batteries. The packaging and products also lack warnings required under Reese’s Law – a federal law signed in 2022 that sets mandatory safety standards to prevent children from swallowing button cell or coin batteries. 
 If swallowed, button cell and coin batteries can cause serious injuries, including internal chemical burns, and can be fatal.
 About 229,430 units were included in the recall. No injuries or incidents have been reported.
 Recalled tools sold at Amazon, Lowe’s, other retailers
 Dig deeper:
 The recalled products were sold at Lowe’s Home Improvement, Menards, W.W. Grainger, True Value Hardware and other hardware stores nationwide, as well as online at Amazon.
 The recalled products were sold at major hardware retailers and online, including Lowe's and Amazon. (Credit: Justin Sullivan/Getty Images) 
 The Johnson Level digital angle locators, digital calipers and building calculators were sold from February 2023 through November 2026 for between $64 and $400.
 RELATED:  Nearly 17,000 youth bike helmets recalled over risk of serious injury or death 
 The CLC Lighted Portfolio and Johnson Level 7-inch Digital Angle Locator and Ruler were sold from March 2024 through November 2026 for between $45 and $55.
 Seet the  recall details , including the model and UPC codes,  here .
 Consumers should stop using recalled trade tools
 What you can do:
 CPSC said that consumers should immediately stop using the recalled products, keep them out of reach of children and contact the manufacturer Hultafors Group North America for a refund.
 To receive a refund, consumers must upload a photograph of the product at   www.HG2026.expertinquiry.com and certify that it has been disposed of and will no longer be used. After verification, consumers will receive a virtual Visa gift card for the product's retail price.
 Consumers should dispose of button cell batteries or recycle them according to local hazardous waste procedures.
 The Source: The information for this story was provided by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) on Nov. 19. This story was reported from Los Angeles.
